title: Air Canada chatbot bereavement fare
organization: Civil Resolution Tribunal of British Columbia; Air Canada

cells.title: Source
body: The Civil Resolution Tribunal of British Columbia issued Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, on February 14, 2024. The decision concerned a passenger who relied on information from Air Canada's website chatbot about bereavement fares.
The ruling is the primary artifact. It records the chatbot statement, the contradictory webpage policy, Air Canada's submissions, and the damages order.

cells.title: Observed behavior
body: The chatbot told Jake Moffatt that a ticket could be submitted for a reduced bereavement rate after travel, within 90 days of ticket issuance. Air Canada's bereavement travel webpage said the policy did not apply after travel had been completed.

Moffatt relied on the chatbot statement, booked flights, and later sought a partial refund. Air Canada denied the refund and argued that it could not be held liable for information provided by the chatbot.

cells.source: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, paragraph 15
cells.context: Chatbot response quoted in the ruling
cells.output: If you need to travel immediately or have already travelled and would like to submit your ticket for a reduced bereavement rate, kindly do so within 90 days of the date your ticket was issued by completing our Ticket Refund Application form.

cells.source: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, paragraph 17
cells.context: Air Canada webpage policy described in the ruling
cells.output: The webpage says, in part, the bereavement policy does not apply to requests for bereavement consideration after travel has been completed.

cells.source: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, paragraph 27
cells.context: Tribunal characterization of Air Canada's chatbot-liability argument
cells.output: In effect, Air Canada suggests the chatbot is a separate legal entity that is responsible for its own actions. This is a remarkable submission.

cells.source: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, paragraphs 40-44
cells.label: Order

cells.title: Provenance
body: Primary source: CanLII copy of Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149.
The ruling identifies the source as the Civil Resolution Tribunal of British Columbia, dated February 14, 2024, file SC-2023-005609.
No secondary source is needed to identify the artifact.

cells.title: Notes
body: The underlying chatbot screenshot is described in the decision. The case file quotes only the parts of the screenshot reproduced in the ruling.
The decision states that Air Canada did not provide information about the nature of its chatbot.
